How a design splits its sample over the strata of a frame

Source: R/design-stratified.R
allocation_table.Rd

The rows draw() takes from each stratum, the inclusion probability that gives each row there, and the reason for any stratum held at the floor, capped at its size or left with no rows, all before anything is drawn. Under Neyman allocation it also shows the standard deviation of each stratum the split used, and the cost per row when the design has costs. The numbers come from the same computation as draw() and inclusion_prob(), so they always agree with both.

Usage

allocation_table(data, design)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

design

design_stratified(), design_spread() or design_weighted() with strata, or design_certainty() whose rest is one of these. For the last the table describes rest over the rows below the threshold, and the rows at or above it, which are taken with certainty, are not counted in any stratum. Other designs are refused.

Value

A data frame with one row per stratum of data, in key order (see design_stratified()): the strata columns, then

N

Rows in the stratum.

n

Rows drawn from it.

prob

The inclusion probability of each of its rows, as inclusion_prob() gives it. NA for design_spread() with size and for design_weighted(), whose rows in one stratum have different probabilities; there inclusion_prob() gives them row by row.

sd

Under Neyman allocation, the stratum's standard deviation that the split used: of the allocation_by column within the stratum, or as given. NA under other allocations.

cost

The cost of one row, when the design has cost, and NA otherwise.

status

Why the stratum got n: "rule" for its share under the allocation rule, rounded; "count" for a count given in allocation; "floor" for a stratum raised to min_per_stratum from a smaller share; "capped" for one the rule asked more rows of than it holds, so it is taken whole and the rows it could not give go to the other strata; "take-all" for one taken whole for another reason, such as a size below min_per_stratum or a count equal to its size; and "empty" for one allocated no rows, whose rows can never be drawn. With replace = TRUE no stratum is capped or taken whole.

See also

design_stratified(), design_spread(), inclusion_prob()

Examples

df <- data.frame(id = 1:300,
                 site = rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), c(150, 100, 45, 5)),
                 v = c(1:150 %% 7, 1:100 %% 19, 1:45 %% 3, 1:5 * 40))
d <- design_stratified("site", n = 30, allocation = "neyman",
                       allocation_by = "v", min_per_stratum = 2)
allocation_table(df, d)
#>   site   N  n       prob         sd cost status
#> 1    a 150  8 0.05333333  1.9948592   NA   rule
#> 2    b 100 15 0.15000000  5.5331873   NA   rule
#> 3    c  45  2 0.04444444  0.8257228   NA  floor
#> 4    d   5  5 1.00000000 63.2455532   NA capped

# The same counts as a draw, and the same probabilities as inclusion_prob()
table(draw(df, d, seed = 1)$site)
#> 
#>  a  b  c  d 
#>  8 15  2  5 
tapply(inclusion_prob(df, d), df$site, unique)
#>          a          b          c          d 
#> 0.05333333 0.15000000 0.04444444 1.00000000
